svg.title: Hermes’ Delivery Office, ancient drawing
svg.desc: Fictional AWS architecture. Tenant A and B are illustrative customers. Workload roles sign PutEvents; resource policies and an account-to-tenant allowlist constrain ingress and routing. Multi-tenant publishers within a single customer account would need a separately validated ingress contract. AZ A/B contain private Fargate tasks, not independent SQS or DynamoDB instances. Assumed SQS interface endpoints have ENIs in enabled AZs; DynamoDB uses a gateway endpoint. Endpoint and security-group configuration is not drawn. Cross-account bus forwarding requires a sender role, destination bus policy and explicit target permissions. Dedicated workers have no intended pooled-state access. These policies are design requirements, not validated IAM documents. Queue arrows denote polling and configured redrive. Consumers need idempotency, tenant-scoped state access and a privileged, audited replay process. A shared queue is a noisy-neighbour trade-off; stricter service tiers may need more queue partitions. Recipient transport and autoscaling policies are omitted. Tenant A publisher to Authorized ingress; Tenant B publisher to Authorized ingress; Operator sign-in to Tenant controller; Tenant controller to Authorized ingress; Authorized ingress to Pooled delivery queue; Pooled delivery queue to Delivery tasks A; Pooled delivery queue to Delivery tasks B; Delivery tasks A to Pooled tenant ledger; Delivery tasks B to Pooled tenant ledger; Pooled delivery queue to Pooled failed work; Authorized ingress to Tenant B ingress; Tenant B ingress to Tenant B queue; Tenant B queue to Tenant B worker; Tenant B worker to Tenant B ledger; Tenant B queue to Tenant B failed work. Boundary labels distinguish accounts, regions, VPCs, AZs, subnets and logical groups. These annotations do not verify deployed isolation or permissions.

g.title: SigV4 PutEvents under Tenant A workload role; bus policy restricts allowed principal/account and source.
Tenant B publishes under its own role; account-to-tenant bindings are configured by the platform.
Authenticated operator JWT authorizes tenant administration; this is credential flow, not a Cognito RPC.
Installs allowlisted account-to-tenant routes; do not trust a tenant ID supplied in event detail.
Rules select the pooled tenant route and deliver through a queue resource policy.
Private tasks poll SQS over a configured interface endpoint; delivery is at least once.
A second AZ runs independent consumers of the regional queue.
Conditional idempotency records and tenant-keyed state via a DynamoDB gateway endpoint.
Same regional tenant ledger; no per-AZ DynamoDB clone is implied.
Configured redrive after unsuccessful receives; controlled replay is a separate operation.
Cross-account EventBridge forwarding needs a sender role and destination bus policy.
Dedicated account queue receives only the allowlisted Tenant B route.
Lambda event-source mapping polls the dedicated regional queue.
Dedicated state and execution role; no pooled-data access is required.
Dedicated redrive destination with an explicit source-queue allow policy.
